description: The render_visual arguments. Also the source of the input schema the host sees.

subtitle.description: Optional subtitle, plain text, e.g. the unit and period: 'EUR, FY2025'.

chart_type.description: variance compares actuals with a scenario (needs Val plus PY, PM, PL or FC); bar and pin show one series; waterfall shows contributions; line and area show trends over time.

category_columns.description: Category column(s). One column, or up to 5 for a hierarchy (parent first, e.g. Region, Country, City). A time axis cannot be part of a hierarchy. Use more than one column ONLY for a parent-child hierarchy, where every child value belongs to exactly one parent (e.g. Country > City). For two independent dimensions, whose values repeat under each other (e.g. Region and Channel), put the one with fewer values in group_columns (groups) instead.

time_axis.description: Set when the category column is a time period, so it is drawn as a chart: year for integer years (2025), semester for half-years (H1 or 2025-H1), quarter for quarters (Q1 or 2025-Q1), month for month names (Jan or January), yearmonth for YYYY-MM (2025-01), date for days as YYYY-MM-DD (2025-01-31). Send the rows in time order. Leave it out for any other category.

group_columns.description: Optional column(s) that split the visual by a second dimension. On a chart (a time_axis category) each group value gets its own small chart, and two columns give a grid (first = rows, second = columns); in a table each group value gets its own columns with a total. Send one row per category and group combination. Use a time period as a group only without time_axis. About 6 groups read well.

measure.description: Measure on the value axis. Values are column names from columns.

name.description: Display name of the measure, e.g. 'Revenue'.

PM.description: Column with previous-month values. Use either PY or PM, not both.

PL.description: Column with plan or budget values.

additional_measures.description: Optional columns of further measures to show next to the measure, e.g. Units or Margin %. Each is labelled with its column name and shows actuals only. A table shows every one as its own column; a chart shows only the first, as a second series.

negative_impact.description: True when an increase of the measure is bad, e.g. costs or expenses. Flips the variance colours.

sort_by.description: Scenario or variance to sort categories by. Ignored for a time_axis and line or area charts.

rows.description: Pre-aggregated rows in the order of columns, one per category combination.

totals.description: Optional totals, computed from the source data, for measures whose totals are not the sum of their rows: ratios such as Margin %, averages, and stock values such as headcount or balances. Leave it out when every measure sums, like revenue, costs or units; those totals are summed from the rows automatically. One row per total in the order of columns, with null in each category or group column the total spans: with category columns Region, Country, [Europe, null, ...] is the Europe total and [null, null, ...] the grand total. Fill the measure columns that don't sum and leave the others null. A measure column with totals needs one for the grand total and every parent category; with group_columns also for every group total, i.e. every combination of rows with nulls at the end of the category columns, the group columns, or both.
